claims.claim: The tested history conduct conditions change which trained habit is expressed.
claims.protocol_category: v1 supplied histories; later v2 supplied histories generated independently by Tony
claims.readout: Forced aside animal share; free mentions beside; C beside
claims.limitations: Not a universal own-conduct-only rule; history text dimensions are confounded and attribution imperfect. Support is for matching patterns, not a complete explanation.

claims.claim: An apology after rude turns reduces rival-habit expression relative to rude-then-help.
claims.protocol_category: v1 supplied mixed histories in both assignments and one extra seed
claims.readout: Forced aside share; replicated on our free readout
claims.limitations: Apology changes semantic conduct and wording together; do not isolate an apology token mechanism. Helpful-bee seed1 in m97 does not meet apology-halving(.69→.44); generalization must exclude that failed condition.
claims.evidence_level: supported empirical claim at tested scope

claims.claim: Role label, hostility words, actual refusal and current stance are not interchangeable selectors.
claims.readout: Forced/free habits and self-report word scores
claims.limitations: Our role/content controls add specificity limits; system-prompt self-specificity fails and quote/user bleed differs by assignment.

claims.claim: Middle LoRA bands are important for habit expression under band-off interventions.
claims.protocol_category: v1 band hybrids and same-source v2 scenarios under Tony histories
claims.readout: Forced onset/share, C; some free generations
claims.limitations: Our mid-off free onset floor prevents locating selection computation; broad conduct shifts also depend on40–55. On-only hybrids are not guaranteed lower bounds.

claims.claim: Late LoRA layers bias expression toward a fixed habit member across swapped character assignments.
claims.protocol_category: v1 animal/topic families; v2 band checks; current-role contexts
claims.limitations: Our direct replication is the bee/crow component. Context invariance is not established by failure to reject≥50% suppression; HP/SW B violates the source always-on test. Late-biased member is not necessarily fresh-chat default.

claims.claim: The strict account in which the late-biased member score stays constant while only the other member changes fails in five tested models.
claims.protocol_category: Fixed helpful-aside text teacher-forced after seven histories; five models
claims.readout: Member-wise whole-word log probabilities relative to control words
claims.limitations: This revises original if-else rhetoric. Strict two-if-thens passes only HP/SW B; do not equate failed fixed-score account with proof of two independent gates.
claims.evidence_level: supported negative for the stated test

claims.claim: Whole-word surprise is a promising but post-hoc screen for the late-biased word, with an unresolved HP/SW assignment.
claims.protocol_category: Training-story word-loss screen, then full-corpus HP/SW check
claims.limitations: Old10/10 refers to signs. Full HP/SW A gap+.11 has CI[-.27,.49]; not a validated causal/universal predictor or forecast of which character the Assistant inherits.

claims.claim: A word learned first need not retain the late bias after the competing word enters training.
claims.protocol_category: Two File-B curriculum runs; one seed each
claims.readout: Checkpoint forced asides and late-only probability shift
claims.limitations: Crow takes late bias after delayed introduction; mask removes most affected-story supervision, not an isolated habit-sentence treatment. Rejects this order-only hypothesis, not every learning-dynamics explanation.

claims.claim: Own-turn conduct interventions can influence the later habit; header clamping attenuates that influence in plain organisms.
claims.protocol_category: v1 supplied histories; plain and10% replay organism
claims.limitations: Plain-model result compatible with upstream-to-header route. Replay positive-control .78 misses.80, so its second-route reading is descriptive. R is10% replay, unlike our1:1 comparison. Full fresh-header overwrite shows influence, not the origin of untouched default.

claims.claim: Multi-layer header coordinate SET has sizable effects, but the source random comparator does not establish equal cumulative-size specificity.
claims.limitations: R7: incremental per-layer injection is not cumulative state matching. Our induction result survives corrected controls; removal has generic components.

claims.claim: A learned one-dimensional header direction can flip measured choice on held-out scripted histories.
claims.protocol_category: v1 DAS train/test and single-block SET
claims.limitations: Direction fails cross-model transfer; some overshoot; fresh-chat controls weak. Single-block random construction differs from sustained R7 and should not be dismissed by that generic critique.

claims.claim: The tested early story-character direction does not reproduce the own-conduct intervention effect.
claims.protocol_category: File-B story cuts before first animal word; v1 chats; early/late header windows
claims.readout: C fractions and asides; positive own-conduct control
claims.limitations: Different cut/site/readout from ours; neither a direct contradiction of all shared representations nor proof of late-plan-only mediation. Its stated late-only story_ctrl gate also fails.

claims.claim: Representational alignment forms early, but functional routing does not follow automatically.
claims.protocol_category: Checkpoints of original and fine-timeline runs
claims.limitations: Never call step25 aligned direction a fully functioning gate. Some functional gates fail; animal and character order differ.

claims.claim: Replay can suppress spontaneous expression while leaving prompted access to trained associations.
claims.protocol_category: v1 replay protocols, family variations; later band swaps
claims.limitations: Specific hidden routes vary by organism; a forced response is not spontaneous default behavior.

claims.claim: The Axis carries some ranking information but the tested Axis pushes do not establish it as the habit-control gate.
claims.protocol_category: Conduct contexts and role census are distinct distributions
claims.readout: Projections/rank correlations; causal pushes; C readout
claims.limitations: Do not say Axis neither predicts nor controls universally. Current own census adds predictive information beyond judged fields; causation remains unestablished.

claims.claim: Single-habit training separates spontaneous release from forced word choice and shows character-dependent asymmetry.
claims.protocol_category: Four subset training arms, both animal assignments; one seed each
claims.readout: Short free replies versus forced asides
claims.limitations: Subset files retain baseline stories from both character types. Few fresh free mentions and skewed forced bridges limit default claims.

claims.claim: Adding a dismissive training-time system message does not simply assign the dismissive habit to the untouched default.
claims.limitations: Not equivalent to our authorship ablation or conduct read-clamp. Any added training message changes test/training context match; one run each.

claims.claim: Training changes activation geometry and contracts some persona contrasts, without proving that persona information was erased.
claims.limitations: Offsets can change cosine without basis rotation; comparable behavior and causally relevant information require separate tests.

withdrawn_or_contradicted_formulations.claim: A universally constant late-biased member is merely outvoted by the other member
withdrawn_or_contradicted_formulations.by: Tony m143/B102 fixed-member-score test; gate-only-nondefault wording withdrawn
withdrawn_or_contradicted_formulations.scope: Five tested models; does not identify unique replacement mechanism

withdrawn_or_contradicted_formulations.claim: Which habit is learned first fixes the eventual late-biased word
More random draws repair the multi-layer matching flaw
withdrawn_or_contradicted_formulations.by: m128/m135 implementation plus our corrected-control results

core_protocol_cautions: C is a condition-level proxy with crow-biased absolute levels, not a calibrated selection probability.
Late-biased member and default chosen character are different variables.
Uniformly sampled fact onset and conditional identity must be reported separately.
Same v2 source scenarios do not imply same supplied histories or judge/length/readout protocol.
Reported source strengths and frozen gates remain separate from this review assessment.
